mainTopic: Whether a מחיצה can create an איסור (אביי's principle of סילוק מחיצות), and רב יהודה's rulings on when people in three adjoining קרפיפות count as a שיירא.
overview: The amud opens in the middle of a debate: can putting up a מחיצה ever create an איסור? A ברייתא about a סוכה on an אכסדרה with פצימין is raised against אביי. אביי answers that in his view the סוכה is still כשרה, and that even in the other view the problem is סילוק מחיצות, the removal of a partition that used to exist. רבה בר רב חנן challenges him with a ברייתא about vines and seeds in a half-roofed house, and אביי gives the same answer. רבא then sends a ברייתא showing that vineyard walls can make the law stricter. אביי points to a משנה about קרחת הכרם and מחול הכרם. He explains that the strictness comes from the vines' four-אמה work area and from the abandoned strip along the fence, not from the wall creating an איסור. Next, רב יהודה rules on three קרפיפות side by side: depending on which enclosure is wider, three people either count as a שיירא with unlimited space or get only six בית סאה. The גמרא asks two follow-up questions about uneven numbers of people and rules that both are decided leniently. Finally, רב חסדא begins a new statement that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof from a סוכה on a portico with posts
steps.stepSummary: A case from הלכות סוכה is brought to show that adding a partition can turn something כשר into פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone put סכך on top of a portico that has posts, the סוכה is כשרה. But if he evened out its posts, it is פסולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a case from סוכה as evidence that a partition can cause an איסור. A portico with sticking-out posts makes a valid סוכה, but once the posts are evened out by building walls next to them, the סוכה becomes invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אכסדרה has two real walls, and the corner posts (פצימין) sticking out count as closing off the open sides. When he builds alongside them so the posts no longer stick out, something was added, yet the result is פסולה. The claim is that adding construction produced a prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: He put on the סכך (the roofing of a סוכה)
Portico, a roofed porch area that is open on some sides
Posts at the corners that stick out like doorposts
He evened out, made flush or level
Valid / invalid

steps.confusionAlert: Evening out the posts means he ADDED wall material next to them so they no longer stick out. He did not remove the posts. That is exactly why this looks like a case where adding something causes a prohibition.

phrases.english: If one placed roofing on top of a portico
that has protruding posts, it is valid.
phrases.notes: The posts count as closing off the open sides.

phrases.english: But if he evened its posts, it is invalid.
phrases.notes: He built walls flush with the posts, so they no longer stand out.

steps.triggerLanguage: סִיכֵּךְ עַל גַּבֵּי אַכְסַדְרָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ פַּצִּימִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion on the daf about whether a partition can create an איסור, bringing a case from סוכה as evidence.
steps.raayaObject: That a מחיצה (added construction) can create an איסור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of סכך placed on an אכסדרה with פצימין, which becomes פסולה once the פצימין are evened.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's position that a מחיצה never creates an איסור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Evening the פצימין adds construction, and the סוכה turns from כשרה to פסולה. That looks like an added partition creating an איסור.

steps.title: אביי: it is really the removal of partitions
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof. In his view the סוכה stays כשרה, and even in the other view the problem is the loss of the original partitions.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: In my view it is valid. In your view, it is a case of removing partitions.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on the proof in two layers. First he says he does not accept the ruling at all. Second, even if it were פסולה, a new partition is not the cause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In אביי's own view the evened סוכה is still כשרה, so there is no proof at all. In the other view it is פסולה, but only because evening the posts erased the partitions the posts had been creating. The cause is the removal of a valid partition, not the addition of a new one.

keyTerms.meaning: According to me, in my view
According to you, in your view
Removal of partitions, cancelling existing walls

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of סילוק מחיצות becomes אביי's main tool. It lets him say that a partition never creates an איסור by itself; an איסור only comes from taking away a partition that used to permit.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
In my opinion, it is valid,
according to you, it is a removal of partitions.
phrases.notes: The partitions the posts made were just taken away; no new partition is what made it invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: לְדִידִי כְּשֵׁירָה, לְדִידָךְ סִילּוּק מְחִיצּוֹת הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Full rejection. אביי denies the ruling in his own view, and in the other view he reinterprets why it is פסולה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the added construction caused the invalidity. Really, the invalidity comes from erasing the original partitions.

steps.title: Challenge from vines in a half-roofed house
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב חנן brings a ברייתא about כלאים in which extending a roof makes sowing אסור, which seems to show a partition creating an איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב חנן said to אביי: Don't we find that a partition can cause a prohibition? It was taught: In a house that is half roofed and half not roofed, if there are vines here, it is permitted to sow there. But if he evened its roofing, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא challenges אביי with a ברייתא. In a half-roofed house, vines under the roof and seeds in the open part are allowed. Once the roof is extended over the whole house, sowing becomes אסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When half the house is roofed, the edge of the roof is treated as if it comes down and forms a wall (פי תקרה יורד וסותם), which separates the vines from the seeds, so there is no כלאים. Extending the roof adds more roofing, and suddenly sowing is forbidden. This looks like adding something that creates an איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: A partition that creates a prohibition
Roofed, covered
Grapevines
To sow seeds, relevant to כלאי הכרם
Its roofing

steps.confusionAlert: Here the roof itself acts as the partition. The roof's edge is pictured as coming down to the ground and making an invisible wall between the two halves.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה בַּר רַב חָנָן לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Hanan said to Abaye:
And didn't we find a partition causing prohibition?
But wasn't it taught: A house, half of which is roofed
and half of which is not roofed,
with vines here (under the roof), it is permitted to sow there (in the open part).
phrases.notes: The roof's edge acts as a partition separating them.

phrases.english: But if he evened its roofing, it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: He extended the roof over the whole house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אביי deflects the סוכה proof, a new challenge is brought from כלאים.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's position that a partition does not create an איסור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Adding roofing turned a permitted situation into a forbidden one, which seems to be a partition causing an איסור.

steps.title: אביי: there too it is removal of partitions
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that in the vineyard case as well, the איסור comes from removing the roof-edge partition.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There too, it is a removal of partitions.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the same answer he gave before. Extending the roof did not create a new forbidding wall. It erased the imaginary wall that the roof's edge used to make.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the extension, the roof's edge made a partition between the vines and the seeds. Once the roof covers everything, there is no edge, so that partition is gone and the vines and seeds share one space. The איסור comes from losing the separating partition, not from adding one.

keyTerms.meaning: There, in that case

steps.whatToRemember: אביי consistently holds that a מחיצה never creates an איסור by itself. Every case that seems to show this (the סוכה on the אכסדרה, the half-roofed house with vines) is explained as סילוק מחיצות, the removal of a partition that used to permit.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם סִילּוּק מְחִיצּוֹת הוּא.
phrases.english: He said to him: There, it is a removal of partitions.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם סִילּוּק מְחִיצּוֹת הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 by applying the same principle אביי used in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Full rejection of רבה בר רב חנן's proof.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge assumes the extra roofing created the איסור. Really, the extension removed the roof-edge partition that had been separating the vines from the seeds.

steps.title: רבא sends a challenge: vineyard partitions can be lenient
steps.stepSummary: רבא sends a message to אביי through רב שמעיה בר זעירא, quoting a ברייתא that says vineyard partitions can be lenient or strict. It first explains the lenient case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא sent a message to אביי through רב שמעיה בר זעירא: Is it true that we never find a partition that creates an איסור? But a ברייתא teaches: Partitions in a vineyard can make things easier or stricter. How? If a vineyard is planted right up to the base of a wall, one may sow on the other side of the wall, starting right from its base. Without a wall, he would have to stay four אמות away before sowing. This is how vineyard partitions make things easier.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges אביי's rule that a partition never creates an איסור. This step quotes the beginning of the ברייתא, the lenient half, and sets up the strict half that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says partitions work in two directions. The lenient case is not a problem for אביי, because the wall only separates the vines from the seeds. The real challenge is in the strict half, which comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Through, by means of (sent with a messenger)
The partitions or walls of a vineyard
To make lenient and to make strict
The base of the partition
He must keep a distance of four cubits

phrases.english: Rava sent to Abaye
through Rav Shemaya bar Ze'eira:
And have we not found a partition that creates a prohibition?
phrases.notes: רבא is quoting אביי's claim in order to attack it.

phrases.english: But it was taught in a baraita:
Partitions of a vineyard can make things lenient and stringent,
How so?
A vineyard planted right up to the base of a partition:
one may sow from the base of the partition and onward (on the other side).
For if there were no partition there,
he would distance four cubits and then sow,
and this is how vineyard partitions are lenient.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רָבָא לְאַבָּיֵי בְּיַד רַב שְׁמַעְיָה בַּר זְעֵירָא: וְלֹא מָצִינוּ מְחִיצָה לְאִיסּוּר? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge against אביי's position, after he deflected רבה בר רב חנן's כלאים challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that a partition never creates an איסור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא openly says vineyard partitions can be strict. This step quotes the lenient half to set up that point.

steps.title: The strict case: a wall eleven cubits from the vineyard forbids sowing
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's strict case: if a vineyard ends eleven אמות from a wall, one may not sow in that space. Without the wall, he would only need to stay four אמות away.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how are partitions strict? If the vineyard was eleven אמות away from a wall, he may not bring seeds into that space. Without the wall, he would only need to stay four אמות away and then sow. This is how vineyard partitions make things stricter.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the heart of רבא's challenge. Because the wall is there, the space between the vines and the wall becomes forbidden for sowing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no wall, keeping four אמות from the vines would be enough. The wall closes off the strip, so a strip narrower than twelve אמות counts as part of the vineyard and cannot be sown at all. Here the wall seems to be what creates the איסור, which goes directly against אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: Set back from the wall
He may not bring seed there (may not sow there)
For if it were not so

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the clearest case so far of a partition seeming to create an איסור. אביי's whole position depends on how he handles it.

phrases.english: And to be stringent, how so?

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה מָשׁוּךְ מִן הַכּוֹתֶל אַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה —
phrases.english: If the vineyard was set back eleven cubits from the wall:
one may not bring seed there,
for if there were no partition,
he would distance four cubits and sow,
and this is how vineyard partitions are stringent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא started in step 5 and gives the case that actually challenges אביי.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's rule that a partition does not create an איסור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without the wall, sowing beyond four אמות would be allowed. With the wall, it is forbidden. So the wall itself seems to create the איסור.

steps.title: אביי: you could have challenged me from a stronger source, a משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי replies that by רבא's logic, he could have asked from a משנה. He quotes the משנה about the sizes of קרחת הכרם and מחול הכרם.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: By your reasoning, challenge us from a משנה! As we learned: For a cleared patch in a vineyard, בית שמאי say twenty-four אמות and בית הלל say sixteen אמות. For the bare edge of a vineyard, בית שמאי say sixteen אמות and בית הלל say twelve אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי does not answer directly yet. He points out that a משנה shows the same kind of strictness, which sets up his answer: whatever explains the משנה also explains the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "ולטעמיך" means "by your own logic." אביי is saying that if this pattern really proved that partitions create איסור, a well-known משנה would have proven it already. Since the משנה is clearly not about partitions creating איסור, the ברייתא does not have to be read that way either.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your own reasoning
Challenge us from a משנה
A "bald spot" of a vineyard: a cleared area in its middle
The bare strip around the edge of a vineyard

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not agreeing that the challenge works. He brings the משנה to show that this kind of measurement rule has nothing to do with partitions creating an איסור.

phrases.english: He (Abaye) said to him:
And according to your reasoning, challenge us from a mishna,
as we learned:
A clearing in a vineyard:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: twenty-four cubits,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: שֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה.
phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: sixteen cubits.
The perimeter of a vineyard:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: שֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: sixteen cubits,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה.
phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: twelve cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: אביי responds to רבא's ברייתא by pointing to a stronger parallel source.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Begins to defuse רבא's whole proof from vineyard partitions.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same strictness appears in a משנה that has nothing to do with partitions creating איסור, so the ברייתא proves nothing about partitions.

steps.title: The משנה defines קרחת הכרם
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains that קרחת הכרם is a vineyard whose middle was destroyed. Under sixteen אמות, no sowing is allowed. At sixteen, he leaves the vines their work area and sows the rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is קרחת הכרם? A vineyard whose middle became bare. If the bare area is less than sixteen אמות, he may not bring seed there. If it is sixteen אמות, he leaves the vines the space they need for their care and sows what is left.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי continues quoting the משנה, which explains what קרחת הכרם means. This prepares the comparison he will draw to רבא's ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, keeping four אמות from vines is enough. In a bare middle area, though, the space must be at least sixteen אמות wide before any sowing is allowed. Only then does he leave four אמות on each side for working the vines and sow the eight in the middle. There is no wall here at all, yet the rule is strict, just like the wall case in the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose middle was destroyed or left bare
Enough space for its work (four אמות for tending the vines)
The remainder

steps.whatToRemember: In קרחת הכרם, sowing is forbidden until the gap is sixteen אמות wide. This is part of the משנה אביי quotes. His actual argument (step 10) is built on the second half, מחול הכרם, where a fence is involved.

phrases.english: And what is a clearing of a vineyard?
A vineyard whose middle was laid bare.

phrases.aramaic: אִם אֵין שָׁם שֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה —
phrases.english: If there are not sixteen cubits there:
one may not bring seed there,
if there were sixteen cubits there:
he gives it (the vineyard) its work area,
phrases.notes: Four אמות alongside the vines on each side.

phrases.english: and sows the rest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's quotation of the משנה and defines the term קרחת הכרם used in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bare middle area of a vineyard may be sown only if it is at least sixteen אמות wide, and then only after leaving the vines their four-אמה work area.

steps.title: The משנה defines the vineyard perimeter
steps.stepSummary: The משנה defines מחול הכרם as the space between a vineyard and its fence. Under twelve אמות, no sowing is allowed. At twelve, he leaves the vines their work area and sows the rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the perimeter of a vineyard? The space between the vineyard and the fence. If there are not twelve אמות there, he may not bring seed there. If there are twelve אמות, he gives the vineyard its work area and sows the rest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה that אביי brought, now the second half about מחול הכרם. This sets up the next step, which explains why this case is no proof against אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a fence, one only needs to stay four אמות from the last vine. With a fence, the space must reach twelve אמות before any sowing is allowed. On the surface, that looks like the fence itself is creating a stricter law.

keyTerms.meaning: The vineyard perimeter: the empty strip between the vines and the surrounding fence
Fence or wall
Enough space for its work area (four אמות for tending the vines)
The remainder, the leftover space

phrases.english: What is the perimeter of a vineyard?
The space between the vineyard and the fence.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם אֵין שָׁם שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה —
phrases.english: For if there are not twelve cubits there,
he may not bring seed there;
phrases.notes: Sowing there would create כלאי הכרם.

phrases.english: if there were twelve cubits there,
he gives it enough for its work area,
phrases.notes: Four אמות next to the vines.

phrases.english: and he sows the rest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה quoted in steps 7-8, moving from קרחת הכרם to מחול הכרם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vineyard perimeter under twelve אמות may not be sown. At twelve, four אמות are left for the vines and the rest may be sown.

steps.title: The fence is not the real reason for the stringency
steps.stepSummary: The real reason is different. The four אמות next to the vines belong to the vineyard's work area. The four אמות next to the fence are abandoned because they are hard to sow. The middle strip counts on its own only if it is four אמות wide.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, there, isn't this the real reason? All four אמות beside the vineyard are the vineyard's work area. As for the four beside the fence, since they are not sown, he abandons them. The space in between: if it is four אמות, it counts as significant; if not, it does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the מחול הכרם law does not show that a fence creates an איסור. So neither this משנה nor רבא's ברייתא is a real challenge to אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The twelve אמות break into three parts: four for the vines, four abandoned along the fence, and four in the middle. If the middle strip is under four אמות, it is too small to stand alone, so it is swallowed into the vineyard and forbidden. In רבא's ברייתא, eleven אמות leaves a middle of only three, so it is forbidden for this reason, not because the wall itself forbids.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the reason
The vineyard's work area
He completely abandons it (treats it as ownerless)
In between, the middle strip
They are significant; they count on their own

steps.whatToRemember: The twelve-אמה rule comes from 4 + 4 + 4. A middle strip smaller than four אמות does not count on its own. So the strictness comes from how the space is measured, not from the fence creating an איסור, and אביי's position stands.
steps.confusionAlert: The fence does matter in practice, but only because people do not bother sowing next to it. That makes the strip beside it abandoned. The fence is not a מחיצה that creates a new איסור.

phrases.english: Rather, there, isn't this the reason:
phrases.notes: This explains why רבא didn't ask from the משנה, and it also answers his question from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: that all four cubits alongside the vineyard
are the vineyard's work area.
Alongside the fence, since they are not sown,
phrases.notes: It is hard to sow right next to a wall.

phrases.english: he totally abandons them.

phrases.aramaic: דְּבֵינֵי בֵּינֵי, אִי אִיכָּא אַרְבַּע — חֲשִׁיבָן,
phrases.english: So the space in between: if there are four, they are significant,
and if not, they are not significant.
phrases.notes: An insignificant strip joins the vineyard and is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the real reason behind the משנה of step 9, which also undoes רבא's ברייתא challenge from step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim, from the ברייתא in step 6, that a vineyard partition can create an איסור
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects both the משנה and the ברייתא as proof that a partition creates an איסור
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The stricter rule comes from the middle strip being too small to count (under four אמות), not from the wall itself forbidding.

steps.title: Three enclosures where the outer two are wider
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules on three קרפיפות side by side, with one person in each. If the outer two are wider and the narrow middle one is fully open to both, all three people count as one שיירא and get unlimited space.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: Three enclosures side by side. The two outer ones extend wider, and the middle one does not. One person is in this one and one in that one. They become like a caravan, and they are given all the space they need.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב יהודה explains when three people in three separate open enclosures are treated as one group with unlimited space.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The middle enclosure is narrower, so it is open along its whole width into each wider outer one. This joins everyone into one shared area. Three people together have the status of a שיירא, which may enclose and use any amount of space.

keyTerms.meaning: Enclosures, fenced open areas
Extending out, wider (so they have wall stubs on both sides of the opening)
The middle one
A caravan (a group of at least three), which may use unlimited enclosed space
All the space they need

steps.whyThisMatters: This applies the earlier principle about a small area breached into a larger one, now with three areas and three people.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
Three enclosures, one beside the other,
and the two outer ones extend wider,
and the middle one does not extend,
phrases.notes: It is open along its whole width into both outer enclosures.

phrases.english: and one person is in this one and one person in that one,
phrases.notes: So there is one person in each of the three.

phrases.english: it becomes like a caravan,
and they are given all the space they need, certainly.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה שְׁלֹשָׁה קַרְפֵּיפוֹת זֶה בְּצַד זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement unrelated to the vineyard debate.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the outer enclosures are wider and the middle is fully open to both, the three people count as one שיירא with unlimited space.

steps.title: Three enclosures where the middle one is wider
steps.stepSummary: Now flip the case: the middle enclosure is wider and the outer two are fully open into it. Then they are not a שיירא, and they are given only six בית סאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the middle one extends wider and the two outer ones do not, and one person is in this one, one in that one, and one in this one, they are given only six בית סאה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives the opposite layout. Here the three people do not become a שיירא, so their space is limited.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the wider middle enclosure is the main area, and the outer ones open into it rather than joining each other. The three do not merge into one group. Instead they get the limited space of individuals, about two בית סאה each, for a total of six.

keyTerms.meaning: An area of six בית סאה (two for each of the three people)
An individual, a single person

steps.whatToRemember: Which enclosure is wider decides everything. If the outer ones are wider, the three people join into a שיירא with unlimited space. If the middle one is wider, they stay individuals and get only six בית סאה.

phrases.english: If the middle one extends wider
and the two outer ones do not extend,
and one person is in this one, one in that one, [and one in this one],

phrases.aramaic: אֵין נוֹתְנִין לָהֶם אֶלָּא בֵּית שֵׁשׁ.
phrases.english: they are given only six בית סאה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶמְצָעִי מְגוּפָּף וּשְׁנַיִם הַחִיצוֹנִים אֵינָן מְגוּפָּפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The reverse case of step 11, with the opposite result.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the middle enclosure is wider, the three people are not a שיירא and get only six בית סאה.

steps.title: One, two, one: do the middle two join one side or split up?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about one person in each outer enclosure and two in the middle. Either side the pair joins makes three, a שיירא. Or perhaps they split, one to each side, so no side ever has three.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: one person here, one person there, and two in the middle. What is the law? If they go out to this side, there are three. If they go out to that side, there are also three. Or perhaps one goes out this way and the other goes out that way?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new question about רב יהודה's setup. This time the people are spread out unevenly: one, two, one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the layout of step 12: the middle enclosure is wider, so the people in it are counted together with one of the outer enclosures. From step 11 we know that three people counted together are a שיירא and get unlimited space. If both middle people go to the same side, that side has three. But if one goes each way, each side has only two. So the question is: which picture do we use?

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before them (the Sages). It opens a real legal dilemma.
The middle one (here, the middle enclosure)
They go out / he goes out (into a neighboring enclosure)
They are three, which is enough to make a שיירא
Or perhaps. It introduces the other side of the question.

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody is actually walking anywhere yet. The question is how to treat the group, based on where the middle people COULD go. Each possible direction gives a different count on each side.

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
One person in this (outer enclosure) and one in that one
and two in the middle one. What is the law?
If they go out to here, they are three,
phrases.notes: Both middle people join one outer person.

phrases.english: and if they go out to there, they are three.
Or perhaps:

phrases.aramaic: חַד לְהָכָא נָפֵיק, וְחַד לְהָכָא נָפֵיק.
phrases.english: one goes out to here, and one goes out to there.
phrases.notes: Then each side has only two people, which is not a שיירא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רב יהודה's second layout from step 12 (middle enclosure wider, outer ones open into it) to an uneven spread of people.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: With people spread one, two, one, do we assume the middle pair joins one side (making three, a שיירא) or that they might split up (making only two per side)?

steps.title: Two, one, two: does the single middle person surely make three?
steps.stepSummary: Suppose we assume the middle pair might split. Now there are two in each outer enclosure and one in the middle. Wherever he goes he makes three, so perhaps it is certain. Or perhaps his unknown direction still leaves the case in doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that one goes this way and one goes that way, what about two here, two there, and one in the middle? Here it is surely fine: if he goes out this way there are three, and if he goes out that way there are three. Or perhaps we say he may go this way, and we say he may go that way?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds a second question on top of the first. Even if splitting up is a concern in the first case, what about a case where splitting is impossible because there is only one person in the middle?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is only one person in the middle, so he cannot split. Whichever way he goes, that side will have three. That suggests a שיירא for sure. The other side of the question asks whether it still matters that we cannot say which side he will join. Without a fixed direction, perhaps neither side is firmly counted as three.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say. It means: even if we accept one answer to the first question, here is a follow-up.
Certainly, for sure
Say (that), it is possible that. It points to an open possibility.

steps.confusionAlert: This second question only comes up IF we take the stricter view in step 13, that the middle pair might split. That is why it begins with 'וְאִם תִּימְצֵי לוֹמַר'.

phrases.english: And if you will say

phrases.aramaic: חַד לְהָכָא נָפֵיק וְחַד לְהָכָא נָפֵיק,
phrases.english: that one goes out to here and one goes out to there,
phrases.notes: This assumes the stricter side of step 13.

phrases.english: then two in this one and two in that one
and one in the middle. What is the law?
Here, certainly,
if he goes out to here, they are three,
and if he goes out to there, they are three.
Or perhaps:

phrases.aramaic: אֵימַר לְהָכָא נָפֵיק, וְאֵימַר לְהָכָא נָפֵיק.
phrases.english: say he goes out to here, and say he goes out to there.
phrases.notes: His direction is not fixed, so we cannot firmly attach him to either side.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּימְצֵי לוֹמַר חַד לְהָכָא נָפֵיק וְחַד לְהָכָא נָפֵיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up question that assumes the stricter answer to step 13 and tests a case where splitting is impossible.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When a single middle person would make three on either side, is that enough for a שיירא, or does his unknown direction keep the case in doubt?

steps.title: The הלכה: these dilemmas are ruled leniently
steps.stepSummary: The questions are not resolved through argument. The final ruling is that both dilemmas are decided leniently, so the people get all the space they need.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is that these questions are decided leniently.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes both questions with a practical ruling instead of a proof. In both cases we follow the lenient side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither question was answered from a source. Still, the ruling is to be lenient. So in the one, two, one case and in the two, one, two case, the people are treated as a שיירא and get unlimited space.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical halacha, the final ruling
Our questions (the dilemmas just raised)
Toward leniency

steps.whatToRemember: With three enclosures where the middle one is wider and the outer ones open into it, a spread of people that could make three in one place is treated as a שיירא. The doubts in steps 13 and 14 are ruled leniently.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that in these doubts about carrying in enclosures (a דרבנן matter), the practical ruling leans lenient even without a clear answer, giving the people all the space they need.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: our questions are decided leniently.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles both open questions from steps 13 and 14 with a practical ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both dilemmas are ruled leniently: the people are treated as a שיירא and given all the space they require.

steps.title: רב חסדא begins a new statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a new teaching from the אמורא רב חסדא. The content of his statement continues on the next amud.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move by naming a new speaker, רב חסדא. Nothing has been ruled yet. His actual words come right after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion of רב יהודה's three קרפיפות has just closed with a lenient ruling on both dilemmas. The formula "אמר רב..." signals that a fresh statement is about to begin. What רב חסדא actually says, and how it connects to what came before, appears only on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: "Said." This word introduces a teaching from a named sage.
A leading Babylonian אמורא, a student of רב.
The standard formula that opens a new מימרא, meaning a sage's own ruling.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not treat this line as a complete teaching. It is only the attribution, and the actual ruling begins on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
phrases.notes: His statement continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the lenient conclusion of step 15 and opens a new statement by a different אמורא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated. The ruling of רב חסדא appears on the next amud.
